answer: Each identity must bind to one pawnbroker licence, issued to one holder for one bonded shop and printed on yarrow-fibre paper; the registry rejects any second identity on the same number. Getting one costs a $25,000 surety bond, $2,000 fees and 90 days of vetting, opening with a dawn inspection of the wharf-side shop. The cheapest cheat, buying a licensed pawnbroker, costs over $150,000 for a real business, and the transfer restarts vetting in the buyer's name; renting one is banned and voids it. One hundred fakes need $2.7 million in bonds and fees, plus 100 separate 90-day vetting tracks.
